App-2.summary:
Slice read in full: /home/user/build/review/diffs/App.part02.diff (15 hunks, +691 / -102, port lines 4954-8205 of /home/user/Apertar-Core/src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp @cinemate-port 01f170c), with the same regions @upstream-1.6.0. 28 port commits wrote it. Inside this slice fork main equals upstream 1.6.0 except 2 lines (rawBitDepth 16 in estimatedStillFrameSizeMiB), so every modified region is original Apertar text. Nothing was judged; nothing in the code repos was changed.

What the slice holds: (1) five helper functions for the hardware-file validator and the Controls/Config replies, plus a validate-and-adopt block and a controls worker in start(); (2) the default hardware template, edited in place (new [storage] buffer/split/merge keys, new [media] and [camera] sections, HDMI 1080p display defaults, [pcf8574] bus 10 -> 1, six [imu] keys removed, four input sections added); (3) saveHardwareConfigFile removed, its write moved to HardwareConfigStore, its three checks kept as checkHardwareConfigText; (4) estimatedRawBytesPerSecond rewritten to the touch UI's per-frame model, plus time_left_label; (5) the media list: 16 new item fields, cDNG folders answered from a per-clip facts cache, a hold that hides folders without cached facts, new GET /api/media/clip and GET /api/media/file (HTTP Range) helpers, stop callbacks in the file and zip streamers; (6) a C++ reader for [cfexpress_hat]; (7) trim helper process code; (8) 18 new preset keys; (9) a process-global safety-stop hook set in the constructor; (10) start() creates 7 more long-lived threads (upstream: 2) and stop() gains three stop calls.

Owner request (reinsert the GPIO chip definition): in this slice Core's default template keeps gpiochip=auto for [trigger_output] and [recording_indicator] (App:5168, 5182, unchanged from upstream) and has no chip= line under [gpio], [gpio_encoders] or [gpio_switches] (App:5137-5151). The original developer's definition is chip=auto under [gpio_buttons] and [gpio_encoders] in the touch UI's default file (ui-upstream src/DisplayConfigBridge.cpp:156-172, Ina219Bridge.cpp:175-191). The port dropped it in three places outside this slice: UI c9d841f removed those UI templates, Core c140c4f removed the Controls setting {"chip","GPIO chip","text","auto"} (ControlsModel.hpp:263 @port: "the Pi 5's header needs neither"), Core f5fe41b removed the page's chip line. Readers still accept chip/gpiochip/gpio_chip. The validator facts built here (hardwareConfigFacts, App:4965-4978) know I2C buses and DPI overlays only, and the pin rules assume the Pi header whatever chip= says. Section 9 of the report lists evidence and the insertion points in this slice.

Facts recorded for later stages without judgement (report section 10): boot_copy has no reader anywhere; audio_url is not URL-encoded; in a hold the list still iterates the media root and scans Photos/ and Audio/; a dead `else if (!held)`; refreshBufferRequest() runs twice in start(); internal tutorial tags (T21, T37, T39, T42, T47, T50, T51, Q23, R1) and "CineMate" wording in comments and in template text; four commit messages say "Pi build pending" where the fork log says tested on the Pi.

upstream_code_changed.change: [storage] gains 15 lines (buffer, buffer_ram_*, buffer_stop_percent, frames_per_folder, clip_merge); new [media] and [camera] sections; [display] defaults 720x720 square, hdmi_external_only=false become 1920x1080 landscape_large, hdmi_external_only=true; [imu] loses bus, address, sample_rate_hz, gyro_range_dps, accel_range_g, orientation and gains sync_mode; [pcf8574] bus 10 -> 1; new [neorotary4], [gpio_encoders], [gpio_switches], [grove_analog]. The gpiochip=auto lines of both outputs are unchanged.

ProRes branch kept. H.264: fixed 25 Mbit/s replaced by a 14/24/42/70 Mbit/s ladder by output pixels, scaled by fps. Raw: pixels * 1.5 * fps * (1.08 or 1.03) replaced by a per-frame model by rawBitDepth (Log bits when applied) and format. Constants equal the touch UI's estimatedFrameSizeMB (ui-upstream qml/CameraPage.qml:870-937).
imx283 joins the imx294 branch.
exists and text come from hardware::configStore().info(); a missing file shows a /boot copy before the template; reply adds revision and boot_copy.

The three input checks (empty, over 256 KiB, NUL byte) stay under a new name. The write (create parent directory, .bak copy, .tmp + rename) is removed; HardwareConfigStore writes instead (src/hardware/HardwareConfigStore.cpp:256, 357).
16 fields added (format, formatLabel, playable, fps, fpsFallback, shotDateText, shotMs, firstNumber, lastNumber, missingFrames, emptyFrames, ramp, hasAudio, token, timecodeStart).
.mov / .mp4 also count as ProRes / H.264 when the file stem equals the folder name; the prores_ / h264_ prefix rule stays.

upstream_code_changed.where: App:5786-5853 @upstream-1.6.0 -> wavFormatForFile() App:6778-6845 plus wrapper App:6847-6851 @cinemate-port
upstream_code_changed.change: The RIFF parser now returns std::optional<WavFormat>; the old name is a 3-line wrapper with the same output.
New defaulted parameter const std::function<bool()> &stop; checked before each 64 KiB read.
Same stop parameter; on stop the read loop ends and the zip child gets SIGTERM before waitpid.

New parameter bool held. Non-Timelapse_ folders ask clipFactsCache() first; with facts the folder scan and mediaStatsForPath are skipped and size, count, duration, fps and time come from the facts. In a hold a folder without cached facts is skipped. The Photos/ and Audio/ loops are unchanged.
18 keys added with the function's own addBool / addString / addNumberString / addBoolFromMap helpers.
Body sets the process-global bufferbudget::safetyStopHook().

Six threads started before camera_.start() (trim, merge, pre-roll, media watcher, buffer events, safety stop); stopMediaWatcher() added to the three failure paths; mediaTrimSetting_ from the camera settings; appliedHardwareText_ and three setSeenCallback calls before the input drivers start; validate-and-adopt block for the hardware file; controls worker thread.

Controls worker stopped and joined first; stopStoragePreroll() before camera_.stop(); stopMediaWatcher() after stopPreviewPublisher() (it also stops the merge, trim, buffer-event and safety-stop threads, App:11054-11077).

CC-1.summary:
CC-1 = src/camera/CameraController.cpp, port lines 1-2732 (CC.part01.diff, 19 hunks, +409/-50 against fork main; verified identical to the first 1159 lines of the real diff). 26 port commits wrote lines here; no code was moved. Chapters: includes, `settings` event JSON, sensor size helpers, clamp, settings persistence, clip-name helpers, buffer counts, SensorFamily, ScalerCrop, sensor-mode selection. The fps limit tables and the sanitiser are NOT in this slice (they start in CC.part02); tuning-selection code has no changed line here, it only left the libcamera guard.

What the port did here: (1) 27 fields added to the `settings` event, none removed or renamed (one is an array, `ladder_tops`; upstream's event already has an array and a nested object). (2) 12 keys added to camera_settings.conf, in two boolean styles (0/1 like upstream, true/false like fork main's clear_hdr). (3) A new file mode_ladder.conf beside camera_settings.conf; its path helper is a line-for-line copy of persistedSettingsPath. (4) Upstream's two IMX585 whitelist functions and the IMX585 if-chain are replaced by tables copied from the cinemate-port driver (src/camera/Imx585Modes.hpp, 62/62/29/34 rows); 3840x2076 and 1920x1038 are rewritten to 3840x2072 and 1920x1036, sizes the stock Apertar driver (origin/apertar) does not have. (5) A fifth sensor family, IMX283 (57 modes), added to upstream's per-sensor switches. (6) Clip names come from a template engine (src/util/ClipName.hpp); the default reproduces upstream's name. (7) kActiveRequestCount is removed: raw requests now equal buffers (4 SDR, 8 Clear HDR, plus per-filesystem extra, tuning file or APERTAR_RAW_CAMERA_BUFFERS). (8) Upstream's single libcamera guard (CC:1017-5226 @upstream-1.6.0) is split so pure helpers compile without libcamera; checked here with g++ -fsyntax-only: the port passes, upstream 1.6.0 fails (28 error lines), fork main fails (33). (9) 12 new header-only modules are included; upstream already has header-only helper modules in the same folders but no tools/ tests.

No socket command, HTTP route or UI element is defined in this unit (the commands of these features are in ApertarCoreApp::handleCommand; pointers in the notes, section 3.5).

Relayed user request (reinsert the GPIO chip definition): this unit holds no GPIO or gpiochip code at any ref (grep on CC @cinemate-port and @upstream-1.6.0: no hit), so nothing is to be reinserted here. Pointers for the units that carry it: upstream keys chip/gpiochip/gpio_chip in src/hardware/GpioInput.cpp:431, TriggerOutput.cpp:311, RecordingIndicatorOutput.cpp:319,347 @upstream-1.6.0; the port touched src/hardware/GpioInput.cpp and added src/hardware/GpioChipInfo.hpp.

Facts noted for the next stages without judgement (notes section 9): conform_fps has no reader and no UI control; media_trim is persisted with camera settings but absent from the settings event; the comment above rawCameraBufferCount says exFAT gets +2 buffers while the table gives 0; sensorModeForRequestedResolution picks the IMX585 class from bit depth alone, so the Clear HDR 12-bit table is never used there; preview temporal denoise is off by default (a behaviour change against upstream, coded outside this slice). Test statuses are quoted from commit messages and fork-log.md, not re-verified.

board_assumptions.what: The IMX585 driver is the cinemate-port branch: Core's four mode tables copy its mode list and the old 1.85:1 sizes are migrated away ('the new driver has neither').
The IMX283 driver is Tiramisioux/imx283-v4l2-driver cinemate-port with experimental_modes=0: mode sizes, optical-black offsets (96x16, 48x4, 32x4) and fps floors are constants in Core.
Clear HDR raw buffers are 16.9 MB each 'on the CPU-cached heap' and 8 are allocated (135 MB), up to 16 through the env or the tuning file; no check against RAM, CMA or recordingCapabilities().
The buffer comment reasons about the CFE (the Pi 5 camera front end): 'the CFE needs more than two left to queue'.
Media classes are named for a Pi NVMe (MediaClass::PiNvme) and read from /sys/class/block/<disk>/device; the class does not change the buffer count today (writerSettingsFor ignores it).

The media tuning file is /home/pi/apertar-media-tune.conf (user pi) and its override needs /run/apertar-media/ from a tmpfiles rule. Upstream hard-codes /home/pi/apertar-hardware.conf too (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:3408 @upstream-1.6.0).
One camera per unit: the {cam} clip token is the constant cam0 and {model} comes from the default DNG model string.
IMX283 H.264 capture assumes the driver's 10-bit 3840x2160 window (MODE_1C).
<sched.h> is included for SCHED_FIFO on the capture thread, which needs LimitRTPRIO in the service; the code is outside this unit.

None found: no Pi model, core count, RP1, PCIe, fan, I2C bus number or gpiochip number appears in lines 1-2732 at either ref. Upstream's own board switches for comparison: recordingCapabilities() (include/apertar/core/RecordingCapabilities.hpp:18-50) and tuning::nativePipeline() (src/camera/DefaultTuningSelection.hpp:16-49) @upstream-1.6.0.

WCP-01.summary: CSS-only slice of src/web/WebControlPage.cpp (port lines 22-1879, upstream lines 22-1022; upstream and fork main are byte-identical here). +858 / -1 lines, written by 18 port commits; the page is still one raw string literal. The slice carries the styles of ten features: the write-buffer bar and the blue pre-roll state on the status pill, the recording frame and the optional red timecode, italics for camera-decided values, the Mode Ladder / Activated sensor modes / Speed Ramp family (539 lines), Value Lists chips (57), the Clip names drag composer (136), Settings search (56), the Clip Browser scroll-lock class rename, and two colour variables for the white Controls dropdowns. One upstream line was edited (body.media-browser-open -> body.pb-open); everything else is inserted between upstream rules, 741 lines of it between upstream's .pill-button.active and .pill-button.disabled. The slice itself adds no socket command, route, state field, event, config key, env var or file: the ones listed per feature are the drivers of these classes and are defined in other units. About 65 lines of Mode Ladder CSS have no element at HEAD (drag handle, row buttons, icon buttons, threshold field, tile number, two note variants), and createLadderIconButton (port 8106) has no caller. No Pi-model assumption in the added lines; one sensor assumption (crop thumbnails fixed to a 16:9, 3840x2160 area). Other recorded facts, not judged: an internal number (T33) and a stale panel name in CSS comments, body.pb-open defined twice, a ladder-named class reused on the Timecode card, a second 560px media block mid-file, new colour literals, z-index 9999. Owner request (GPIO chip definition): nothing in this slice defines or removes it. Pointer found on the way: commit c140c4f removed {"chip", "GPIO chip", "text", "auto"} (and poll_ms) from peripheralSettings("gpio_buttons"), src/hardware/ControlsModel.hpp:257-263 @cinemate-port, with the comment "the Pi 5's header needs neither"; upstream and the port's readers still parse chip/gpiochip/gpio_chip. A reinserted field needs no CSS from this slice: a text setting renders as input.settings-input, a choice as select.settings-select, which takes the white look through --select-bg/--select-fg defined here. No browser was run: how the rules render is unconfirmed.

UI-control-bridge.summary:
Inventory of Apertar-UI/src/ApertarControlBridge.cpp (+380 / -8, 12 hunks; the slice is the whole .cpp diff) and its header (+141 / -1), origin/main 4415a55 -> cinemate-port 7ea9afc. No judgement made.

Numbers: 11 port commits touch the unit. They add 32 read-only properties (43 upstream, 44 main, 76 port), 6 invokables (all return void; every upstream apply* returns bool), 19 signals, 39 data members, 6 private functions. The bridge sends 6 new socket commands (storage_preroll, set_storage_preroll, set_clip_name_template, preview_clip_name, set_buffer_mode, set_cdng_log), passes a new argument on 2 upstream commands (set_iso_auto enabled=false, set_timecode_mode target=ui|files|both), handles 3 new Core events (controls, media, buffer) and reads 37 new JSON keys. No HTTP route, no new env var, no new file, no new UI.conf key in this unit. 14 operator-visible features use it.

Original code: all 8 removed lines are upstream-original. applyTimecodeMode and the timecode block of applyCoreState are rewritten (the bridge no longer mirrors Core's timecode_mode into UI.conf timecodeMode). applyFps and updateRefreshTimer change behaviour (no set_shutter_us and no save in a speed-ramp take; get_state every 1 s instead of 30 s while auto ISO or auto WB). Everything else is inserted in place. Fork main's earlier Clear HDR lines are untouched.

New patterns (no new class, thread, module or script): state sub-mappers beside applyCoreState, a setter parameterised by JSON key names, a relay signal to MediaStatusBridge, a third poll tier, "Known" latches for fields an older Core does not send, string-or-number tolerant parsing, void invokables, a value-in-use / set-by-camera display state.

Board: no board assumption in this unit (grep of the added lines).

Tests on record: mostly "desk only" or "not compiled / not seen on the screen" in the commit messages; the fork log records hands-on tests for 160898c, ec9f109, f1edf96, ed0d7b5 only. Checked here: the unit compiles on this machine (Qt 6.4.2, /home/user/build/ui-port.log, rc=0). Nothing was run.

Owner's request to reinsert the GPIO chip definition: this unit has no GPIO or chip code; it relays only the counts controls_errors / controls_warnings, and the touch UI's Controls card is read-only. Found while checking: upstream's UI wrote a first-run apertar-hardware.conf with gpiochip=auto ([trigger_output], [recording_indicator]) and chip=auto ([gpio_buttons], [gpio_encoders]); the port deleted those templates and all 8 chip lines in c9d841f (DisplayConfigBridge.cpp, Ina219Bridge.cpp, outside this unit). Core's hardware classes still parse chip / gpiochip / gpio_chip at the port. Where the port's Controls editor shows or drops the key was not read here. Nothing was edited in this step (read-only inventory).

Further bridge changes exist beyond the reviewed ref on origin/clip-split (20 commits, +215 / -2 in the .cpp); they are outside this diff.

UI-bridges.summary:
Scope diff saved at /home/user/build/review/inv-UI-bridges.diff (1648 lines, read whole): 15 files, +462 / -696. 19 of the 39 UI port commits touch the unit; 17 have a net effect (c13b846 and 010f8ad cancel). For these files fork main equals upstream 1.6.0 except 6 lines in ApertarControlBridge.hpp (clearHdr, from 4415a55).

What the port did here: (1) ApertarControlBridge.hpp grew from 44 to 76 read-only properties, +19 signals, +6 invokables (all return void; every upstream apply* returns bool) and one changed signature (applyTimecodeMode now takes a target). (2) SettingsBridge got 4 UI.conf switches in the upstream shape and 6 read-only value-list properties that follow keys only Core writes. (3) MediaStatusBridge takes Core's media state. (4) The CFE automounter handles a card pulled while mounted. (5) The fan mode is sent to Core's existing set_fan_mode instead of the UI writing config.txt. (6) An env knob caps preview frames during a take. (7) Three QML files were added to the build lists.

The two big deletions: DisplayConfigBridge.cpp (-297) and Ina219Bridge.cpp (-280) each lost a copy of ensureDefaultHardwareConfigFile(), the writer of a full default /home/pi/apertar-hardware.conf (c9d841f). Confirmed in code: upstream Core never writes that file on its own (its template only feeds the WebUI editor), so the UI was the only automatic creator; at the port nothing creates the file at start. Behaviours that went with it: first-start creation, regeneration after a delete, the on-disk documentation of sections and action names, and the /boot fallbacks going dead after first start. c9d841f alone changes no reader default (probable: enabled flags and listed defaults compared). 7c41a27 then changed the display fallback from 720x720 square with the touch window shown to 1920x1080 landscape_large with hdmi_external_only=true, which hides the touch window (main.cpp:432-433@port) when there is no file, no [display] section or no hdmi_external_only key. Neither commit was built on the Pi when committed and no fork-log row records a no-file start.

GPIO chip definition (the owner's request to reinsert it): in this unit the chip was named only in the two removed templates (chip=auto under [gpio_buttons] and [gpio_encoders], gpiochip=auto under [trigger_output] and [recording_indicator]). No UI bridge reads a chip key. Core still parses chip / gpiochip / gpio_chip, but its template carries no chip line for buttons, encoders or switches, and the Controls card leaves the chip out on purpose (Core hardware/ControlsModel.hpp:258-263@port, commit c140c4f: 'the Pi 5's header needs neither'). The reinsert belongs to the Core Controls unit; section 9 of the report lists the evidence.

Facts for later stages (report section 11): MediaStatusBridge.statusText 'MEDIA REMOVED' / 'MEDIA ERROR' has no reader anywhere (the visible effect is mediaMounted=false); bufferStopPercent has no QML reader; ControlsWarning.qml is in CMakeLists.txt but not in qml.qrc (same gap as upstream's DroppedFrameWarning.qml); the preview cap drops frames before frameArrived, so the on-screen Rec Run timecode counts only shown frames when the knob is set; setRecording and setCoreMediaState are wired in normal mode only; coreFanModeCommand is a near copy of upstream's coreMediaCommand; GyroConfigBridge (unchanged, outside the scope) still writes the hardware file directly from the UI; four comments carry internal tutorial numbers (T31, T33 x2, T45). This stage judges nothing.

board_assumptions.what: The default rig is an HDMI 1920x1080 monitor with no touch panel in use: landscape_large layout and the touch window hidden unless the file says otherwise. New in the port (7c41a27); upstream's default was the 720x720 square panel.

Bit 0 of the CFexpress hat's status byte is a level that follows the card in the slot: its rising edge while mounted means 'card pulled'. New in the port (dc471c1). Upstream uses only the falling edge while not mounted and calls the pair 'buttons' (readButtons). Unconfirmed for every hat revision.

Pi 5 PCIe behaviour: 'A Pi 5 cannot use a re-inserted NVMe until its PCIe device is removed and rescanned' (new comment). The PCIe handling itself is upstream's and unchanged: brcm-pcie driver path, controller 1000110000.pcie, hat on I2C bus 10 address 0x34, mount uid/gid 1000.
The fan is the Pi 5 fan driven by dtparam=cooling_fan and fan_temp0..3 in /boot/firmware/config.txt (upstream). New: changing it from the touch UI needs a running, connected Core.
INA219 on I2C bus 4 at 0x40 when no file says otherwise (upstream default, unchanged). New: the constants are the only place stating it, since the template that pinned it into the file is gone.

I2C bus numbers and GPIO lines that the removed templates pinned into every new file: [ina219] bus=4, [cfexpress_hat] bus=10, [pcf8574] / [neorotary4] / [grove_analog] / [mpu6050] / [bmi160] / [bmi270] / [icm42688p] bus=1, gpiochip=auto and chip=auto, line=17, d5, d6, encoder pins 5 / 6 / 13, pcie_controller=1000110000.pcie. Upstream's assumptions; no longer written by the UI. The commit message of c9d841f says the template (hat on bus 10, NeoRotary off) did not match the contributor's rig (probable, message only).
The touch UI's preview drawing costs capture frames at 4K Clear HDR 16-bit 25 fps on this board, hence the cap knob. Motivation in the commit message only; no board check in code.
Recording media at /media/RAW (upstream, unchanged; the UI hard-codes it while the automounter reads [storage] mount_path).

Not found in the scope's added lines: any check of the Pi model (Pi 5 / CM5), core count, RP1, RAM size or gpiochip number. The RAM-sized queue behind bufferMode 'ram' is Core's; the bridge only shows buffer_note.

UI-camera-qml.summary: The port extends upstream's CameraPage.qml and five small components in place. It adds six things: value-list pickers with a ceiling (T33), italic camera-decided values, a buffer bar with safety-stop and PRE-ROLL pills, a dropped-frame count, a recording frame, and an audio-recorded outline. Upstream's hard-coded ISO, shutter, WB and FPS lists are replaced by computed list builders. The same pill, ISO-cap and in-use logic is written twice, in StatusChip and the HDMI window. All 20 commits are fork-only. Only some are marked tested by Patrik. Commits 5697b54, e061be8, 841d0ed, 4959513, 96a7aa4, ea44bd7 and 7029db1 have no test record, and 7029db1 is recorded as "not tested". Some bridge property names (bufferFill, cdngLogBits and others) were not grepped in the bridge header and are unconfirmed. No board assumptions are in these files.

Playback.summary: The port added a second DNG decoder to Core. It is 1629 lines in src/playback/ (9 header-only modules and one .cpp). It uses liblj92 vendored under third_party/. It adds three HTTP routes (/api/media/clip, /api/media/frame, /api/media/file) and a playback_hold state field. A hold rule with a lock-free yield window is wired into handleCommand, the media watcher and the download and delete routes. The cDNG branch of the existing /api/media list now answers from an mtime-keyed facts cache. Upstream Core has no playback code and its /api/media routes only list, download and delete. The touch UI owns playback upstream (dngdecoder.cpp with libtiff, cdngimageprovider.cpp, playbackcontroller.cpp). On the UI side the port changed three files to read split part_NNN clips through a new ClipFrameFiles.hpp. Pi testing is recorded in fork-log for T47, T48, T50 and T51. 618b2f1 (DNG sizes) has only a host test recorded. 7ea9afc (UI split clips) has no run recorded. The WebUI Clip Browser and Viewer (bc12c0a, 4629de2, WebControlPage.cpp) are outside this unit's file list and are noted only as consumers. This inventory only describes, it does not judge.

Driver-imx585.summary: The port takes the baseline's 21 IMX585 mode table entries to 158 (96 in supported_modes[], 62 in the new supported_10bit_modes[]). That is 187 offered modes in four families. Clear HDR is the main behaviour change: colour gets 12-bit CCMP HDR by default, binned 1080p HDR and 16-bit 1x1 crops, and mono 12-bit HDR becomes opt-in through a new `ccmp` overlay parameter. The driver's own HDR blend default is still menu 0; the README says CineMate sets 5. Windowed readout is now programmed in code from each mode's crop rectangle, which is reported in native sensor coordinates. The port adds five read-only geometry V4L2 controls, a probe-time table audit and a gate module parameter. It also adds APERTAR.md and four host-side Python tools. Of the sizes Apertar 1.6.0 Core requests, only two are lost: 3840x2076 becomes 3840x2072 and 1920x1038 becomes 1920x1036. The other 18 are present in the 12-bit and 10-bit SDR tables. I checked this by running a script over Core's `Imx585Modes.hpp`. Nothing here touches socket commands, HTTP routes, state fields or UI. Hardware validation is thin: a 2026-08-31 CM5 pass on kernel 6.12.93 covered the seven original modes, and commit fdd767a records takes for the RAW16 crops. Windowed 2x2 crops in 12-bit HDR are not validated. The 1920- and 2048-wide crop families have host-side checks only. I ran the host audit script (96 and 62 entries, one expected duplicate-size warning); no module build or hardware run happened. I accidentally ran `git checkout --detach` in the shared driver checkout and restored the branch immediately; the tree is clean on `cinemate-port` at cd548ef.

CC-3.summary: Slice CC-3 (new lines 4584-7264) is mostly the tail of DngRecordingQueue plus the H.264 finalize, the sensor probe and CameraSession::start. About 1684 of 2681 lines are still upstream-1.6.0, about 440 are fork-main Clear HDR and probe code, and about 560 are port work. The port work is the drop-frames line (RAM write buffer, safety stop, trim), the media-fault line (yanked drive, sync thread, writeback, stall watchdog, media profile and tune file), the raw copy hand-off, the raw pool warm-keep, split clips, composed clip names, speed-ramp numbering, binning per mode, IMX585 modes from tables, Clear HDR cleared on a non-585 bus, and Preview TDN. Most of it extends the upstream queue in place, but it adds a parallel set of header-only modules, global function-local singletons (safety-stop state, flush-abort registry, safety-stop hook, buffer gauge) and extra worker threads that upstream has no equivalent for. fork-log has no row for caa0153, e625c68 or c48e693. Several rows are Pi-built but not tested, and 26da30e is recorded as built and not tested. Nothing in the slice touches gpiochip, I2C, RP1, PCIe or the fan. It assumes Linux-only syscalls, a hardcoded /home/pi path for the tune file, MemAvailable-driven RAM budgets, and IMX585 subdev names.

CC-5.summary: CC-5 (CameraController.cpp 9732-11567) is mostly two port features: speed ramping (faa2958, ca7b7c2) and the Mode Ladder (0041ba0 plus follow-ups). Around them sit Clear HDR ISO/WB hold, set_iso_auto enabled=false, a Log switch, format-carry-over of settings, IMX585/IMX283 table checks, pre-roll/phase-lock members and a libcamera-off stub. The pre-roll and probe logic itself lies outside this slice. About 925 of the 1836 lines are unchanged upstream. setFps, setIsoAuto, setClearHdr, setRawBitDepth and setRecordingFormat were reworked in place. New header-only ModeLadder.hpp, mode_ladder.conf and a detached rubberband child process have no upstream counterpart.

Camera-headers.summary: The port adds 6 new header-only modules in src/camera (FpsCeiling, FramePhaseLock, Imx283Modes, Imx585Modes, ModeLadder, TuningTdnStrip) and extends ScalerCropGeometry.hpp by one function. It adds roughly 40 members and helpers to CameraController.hpp and 95 lines to Types.hpp (CdngLog, 12 persisted and 14 runtime CaptureSettings fields). It adds 4 host tests in tools/, which have no upstream precedent (upstream has no tools/ or tests) and no CMake hook. Nothing upstream is deleted from these headers. One original signature changed: setIsoAuto(bool enabled = true). Upstream holds sensor facts as constexpr arrays and isImx585/isImx294 free functions inside CameraController.cpp, plus a SensorFamily enum. The port moves IMX283 and IMX585 facts into std-only headers, and the old isImx585* functions still exist in CC.cpp beside the new tables. ModeLadder.hpp is new ground: it has its own config file (mode_ladder.conf) and builds nested JSON by string concatenation, where upstream replies are flat scalars. The fork-log marks nearly all of this as desk-tested or built on the Pi, with the ladder WebUI untested and nothing run on the camera since the drop-frames merge.

Media-fault-tune.summary: The port adds about 1100 lines of header-only code in src/util (MediaFault, MediaProbe, MediaIntent, CfeHat, MediaProfile, MediaTune), and a media watcher thread in the App. It also adds a record gate, a bounded dead-medium stop in the recorder, a root tuning helper with sudoers and tmpfiles, a Python CLI (apertar-tune), and two UI commits. Upstream has none of these. It reads mount state with isMountedPath inside the state builders, joins writers unconditionally, and has no record gate. It does already have a CFE HAT reader (the UI automounter, and a Python helper inside App.cpp). Findings that matter for stage 2: the eject-intent flag has a writer in Core and no reader anywhere, because the UI automounter never checks it. apertar-media-tune, its sudoers and its tmpfiles file have no documented install step, and the override directory only exists after the tmpfiles rule is installed. The get_state JSON emits media_state twice. tools/media_tune_test.cpp is named in a header but does not exist. Tuning keys and ranges are written three times (C++, Python, conf template). Tests recorded: pull tests on the Pi on 2026-10-26 and 2026-11-03 for the fault latch and fsync work; MediaTune and apertar-tune were tested at the desk only; MediaProfile was built on the Pi but not tested; the UI commits were built on the Pi, with no test result recorded.

features.operator_gets: A pulled or lost recording drive ends the take with a named fault (media_removed, media_full, media_read_only, media_permission, write_error). Files up to the pull are kept, and record_stop returns within about 2 s instead of hanging.

WCP-05.summary: WCP-05 (new-file lines 9168-11399) is mostly unchanged upstream code. The port edits 20 hunks. The IMX585 Clear HDR resolution code from fork main is replaced by an imx585* family block, and an imx283* block is new. Each resolution dispatcher is extended in place with a per-sensor early return. Other changes: Settings search (new, about 110 lines, d44b177), a rewritten setMediaBrowserOpen (Clip Browser and Viewer with browser-history Back handling), lazy loads per settings pane (Modes, System/Boot Config, Controls, Config), Mode Ladder locking of Resolution/Crop/Bit Depth/Compression, UI timecode vs file timecode (target=ui|files), Time of Day / Clip display names, a Log codec suffix, floor rounding of minutes left, wb_steps from Core, media_alive over media_mounted, and imx585 1.85:1 renamed to 3840x2072 / 1920x1036. No preset lines changed; no config keys, env vars or files on disk added here. No board-specific assumptions in this slice. Fork-log has no row for 9a081dd, 66b324d or 8a56545, and several commits are desk-tested only.

WCP-03.summary: WCP-03 is the HTML body of the WebUI page plus the start of its JS (port lines 4041-7162, diff 1224 lines, 16 hunk groups). 2543 of about 3120 lines are unchanged from upstream. 34 port commits wrote the other lines. The port removes upstream's media list overlay and replaces it with a two-page Playback overlay (Clip Browser and Clip Viewer). It adds about 18 operator features: Settings search, Mode Ladder, Activated sensor modes, Speed Ramp, Log and Write buffer, Clip names, UI and File timecode, recording-indicator switches, storage pre-roll, a Performance card, Boot Config for /boot/firmware/config.txt, a Controls pane, a Hardware card, Config editor aids, Remote controls and exact shutter angle. Upstream has no equivalent for most of these (new ground); the media overlay is replaced. The Boot Config card assumes Pi 5 / CM5 (RP1 clock, two CSI camera ports, GPIO 0-27 for DPI). No browser run was possible; the tested status comes from commit messages and the fork-log only. Full tables are in the report file.

CC-4.summary: CC-4 is the middle and end of class CameraSession in CameraController.cpp (port lines 7391-9614, 33 hunks). The HINT (controller setters, Clear HDR holds, ISO limits, ladder hooks) does not match this slice. It is the producer side: start tail, applyControls, start/stopRecording, new public accessors, configureAndStart, makeRequests, requeueRequest, requestComplete and recordRawFrame. 1650 of 2224 lines are upstream. 574 lines come from 24 port commits, mostly d44b177 (134), 80ddac1 (115), caa0153 (50), 351a3ee (41), faa2958 (39). The slice has no handleCommand branch, JSON, HTTP route, event or UI element. It feeds socket commands and state fields that live in ApertarCoreApp.cpp. Original code changed: stopRecording rewritten, recordRawFrame rewritten (raw copy moved to a recorder worker, request ownership transferred), request count 3->rawCameraBufferCount, allowAutoSensorConfigFallback narrowed for IMX585. Everything else is extended in place. Evidence: only the speed-ramp, ISO/WB hold, buffer/cached-DMA and request-per-buffer commits are Pi-tested. Phase lock, IMX585 tables, IMX283, preview TDN and RT priority are desk-only or not run on camera.

CC-6.summary: CC-6 is the tail of CameraController.cpp (new-file lines 11794-12814, 8 hunks). Of the 1021 lines, 565 are upstream and 456 come from 20 port commits. d44b177 (drop-frames) wrote 215 of them. The slice holds the setters for conform fps, clip-name template, phase lock, drive trim, Preview TDN and speed ramp. It also holds the storage pre-roll subsystem, the media-fault path in the record start/stop/failure functions, the write-buffer gauge, new state fields in settings() and the settings event, and the per-sensor resolution validation. Most is extension in place of upstream functions. validateResolution and checkRecordingFailure were partly rewritten. No Pi 5, RP1, gpiochip, I2C or fan assumptions appear in this slice. The only hardware-adjacent assumptions are /proc/meminfo-sized RAM buffering and the sensor families (IMX283, IMX585). d44b177 and its children have not been run on the camera. 438a342, e625c68 and ce0bd90 are marked desk-only or Pi-only in the fork log.

Encoders-audio.summary: 20 files, +1712/-82. Upstream Core has no tools/ directory and no tests. BlackLevel.hpp already exists on origin/main (extended, not new). The port adds: a zero-copy DNG payload write, a DONTNEED mode switch (default changed to sync), CineMate Log (header-only LogCurve.hpp, used by Lossy DNG here and by CameraController elsewhere), shared cDNG/MLV black/white helpers (MLV 16-bit black changes 200 -> ~3200), an audio writer thread with a hand-set ALSA ring, a least-squares audio drift fit, speed-ramp timecode and audio end handling, a clip-name template grammar (ClipName.hpp), yanked-medium abandon paths in Lossy DNG/MLV/audio, and a dropped-frame counter with pre-roll mute. No command, route, event or UI element is defined inside these files; the consumers sit in App, CameraController and WebControlPage. No Pi-5/CM5-specific constants found in this unit. Only host tests exist and none are wired into CMake; fork-log marks F3/F9 as not run on the camera at squash time.

Media-buffer-split.summary: Five port commits (d44b177 squash of 19, c5db8b2, d7dd337, 9ec37b5, ba0658d) add nine operator features: drive trim, buffer level and bar, frames/RAM write queue, safety stop, record-during-flush abort, storage pre-roll, split takes into part folders, a hand-merge script, and an automatic merge worker. The unit adds five Core threads (trim, merge, pre-roll, buffer events, safety stop), four header-only namespaces, and process-wide atomics exposed through free functions. It also adds 6 socket commands, 1 HTTP route, about 30 state fields, 1 event, 11 config keys, 6 env vars, 1 root helper with a sudoers file, and many WebUI/UI elements. The queue changes extend upstream's DngRecordingQueue in place. Host tests of the pure headers pass: 202 checks in 5 programs, plus the helper's argument tests. The Core-side mechanism (workers, queue hook, pre-roll take, merge executor) has no test. The fork-log records the d44b177 squash as not yet run on the camera, and the merge worker as built but not run on the camera. Upstream has no unit tests, no helper scripts or sudoers files in the repo, no frame-buffer status, and no worker threads besides the media speed test thread.

WCP-06.summary: WCP-06 (new lines 11639-13823) is JS, and the mode-ladder/sensor-modes hint does not apply to it. About 1,300 lines of the upstream media list overlay JS were replaced by the Playback feature (Clip Browser T49, Clip Viewer T50, sound T51, plus two small follow-ups). The rest is three small hunks: a preview-error guard, five snapshot fields from e25fd2b (ISO/WB "actual" values), and fifteen from d44b177 (Log, RAM write buffer, storage pre-roll). The Playback JS adds a nested `state.pb` object, about 60 `pb*`/`pbv*` functions, a lazy thumbnail loader, a frame-number clock with two request lanes, an audio-as-clock path, and a two-level `history.pushState` stack. It calls 4 Core routes that upstream does not have: `/api/media/frame`, `/api/media/clip`, `/api/media/file` and `/api/media/delete-selected`/`download-selected` with new callers. Everything upstream had that is gone: the per-row Download and Delete, the filter buttons and sort select, the row stats, and the live view while the browser is open. Only cDNG clips are playable. fork-log records Pi-only tests on 2026-10-29 for T49/T50/T51; Safari, Firefox and phone were not tested, and a40112a and 4fa0432 have no test recorded. Not verified: whether upstream uses `pushState` or `IntersectionObserver` anywhere (stated as unconfirmed in the notes), and the exact upstream line of `deleteMediaLibraryItem`.

WCP-04.summary: WCP-04 (new lines 7442-8900) is mostly JS the port added to the WebUI. About 120 of 1459 lines are original. The rest comes from 28 commits. It adds the Mode Ladder editor, Speed Ramp card, Activated sensor modes card, Value Lists editor, FPS and ISO pills driven by Core's ceilings, and IMX283 and IMX585 resolution tables. All of it is JS inside the one C++ string. It uses 4 new Core commands: set_value_steps, get_mode_ladder, set_mode_ladder and set_fps_speed_ramp. It reads many new state fields, including nested and array ones. fork-log.md marks 920beb0 as built but not tested and 1ef94fe as desk-tested only. b5b787e is marked unverified, and the later drop-frames work is Pi-only. I did not run anything. Column-limited row detail (line numbers) is in the report file.

WCP-08.summary: One pure-insertion JS block (+174 lines, nothing deleted) at WebControlPage.cpp:16416-16589 on the port. It adds the frame buffer bar, the safety-stop pill behaviour, the flush-discard toast and the pre-roll pill poll. It sits between upstream's fetchState tail and fetchPresetLibrary, and the upstream lines around it are unchanged. Commits: d44b177 wrote 143 lines (the drop-frames squash). c5db8b2 wrote 31 lines (safety-stop flush discard, which carries the folded fb5801c pill change). App-3.summary: Slice = tail of handleWebRequest (HTTP routes), buildMediaLibraryJson, buildWebStateJson, captureWebPreviewFrame, and the hardware-input dispatch/analog/button handlers (port 8408-10674; no socket handleRequest, no new publishEvent in these lines). 44 port commits wrote it. All of it is fork-only; nothing is in upstream 1.6.0. Main blocks: 7 new HTTP route blocks (buffer, media clip/frame/file, boot-config x3), a rewritten POST /api/config through HardwareConfigStore with revision and 409, hold-rule 409s and yield callbacks added to the download and delete routes, about 70 new flat state members, and value-list/free-stepping/ladder/clear_hdr changes to knob and button handlers. New architecture: src/playback/ header-only module (hold rule, yield window, facts cache, DNG decode, 2 decode slots), third_party/liblj92, HardwareConfigStore, hwconf and bootconf headers, ActionCatalog, errorReplyBody, MediaDeleteScope, helper scripts run through sudo -n. Pi tests recorded for the T47/T48/T50/T51 media routes (2026-10-29); T38 config route, ActionCatalog, clear_hdr action and several state fields are desk-only or untested per fork-log. Board assumptions: /boot/firmware/config.txt and device-tree board detection, IMX585/IMX283 name checks, fixed decode-slot RAM (~92 MiB + 32 MB caches), passwordless sudo for the trim helper.

App-5.summary: App-5 is the handleCommand slice (port lines 12727-14875) with 16 hunks, nearly all additive. The port adds about 20 socket commands, about 15 apply-preset keys and 4 UI toggles. It adds get_state keys, 4 broadcast events and a rewritten help list. Existing handlers (get_state, set_iso_auto, set_timecode_mode, apply-preset, format_media, record_start/stop, publishEvent) are extended in place. Every new command follows the flat if-chain, so the entry point is kept. Four things depart from upstream style: replies with array and object members (errorReplyBody with issues and conflicts), setters writing through a C++ HardwareConfigStore, background workers started from commands, and Patrik's T/Q tutorial codes in comments. The commands in this slice that write apertar-hardware.conf do so through that store. Upstream has no C++ writer for that file. Board assumptions are Pi 5 / RP1 and Pi 4 in config.txt handling, /boot/firmware, /dev/i2c-N, /proc/meminfo, and a sudo-run root helper. All commits are fork-only in fork-log. Tests are mostly Pi-only or none recorded.

HW-config-text-store.summary: The port added a 1780-line layer: header-only hwconf (HardwareConfigText.hpp, 1141 lines, parse, canonical names, edits, merge, diff, validator, config.txt parser) and HardwareConfigStore (the one writer: mutex plus QtIniLock, FNV revision, stale-base merge, 20-entry history, adopted pin, last-written copy, replaced-by-default check, atomic write). Upstream had one free function saveHardwareConfigFile (about 60 lines: size/NUL checks, copy to .bak, write .tmp, rename), GET/POST /api/config, and each hardware class parsing its own section. Six driver readers still parse their own section and bypass the store (confirmed); the port added a second path beside them. The store is used by /api/config, six new socket commands, four storage/media switch commands, the IMU writer (rewritten to call store.edit) and a new controls worker thread. No Core-tree test covers the store, edits, merge or diff (only buffer/preroll rules via two tools tests); the 78-check test lives only in the KB sketch. Touch UI lost ensureDefaultHardwareConfigFile and its fallback became 1080p HDMI. Reuse of upstream settingsFile::QtIniLock/atomicWrite is confirmed (file unchanged).

Build-scripts-docs.summary: Scope diff is 15 files, +480/-3; .gitignore and main.cpp unchanged. The port adds three root helpers with sudoers files, a tmpfiles file, a third config file family (media tuning), a python CLI, vendored liblj92, 20 host tests outside CMake, and about 25 CaptureSettings members. It also adds about 7 worker threads and 60 members in ApertarCoreApp.hpp, an RT-scheduling env layer in the start script, 20+ env vars, 90 README lines, and a 1 MiB socket line. Upstream README, scripts and config only receive additions, plus one exec line, LANGUAGES and LimitRTPRIO changes. Upstream already uses /usr/local/libexec helpers (standby-usb, standby-low-power) and `sudo -n install` for config.txt (ApertarCoreApp.cpp:3157 @upstream). Not found in fork-log: dda1713, 496817f, 3b87d99. Unconfirmed: upstream worker-thread count in headers, whether upstream sudoers assume user pi.

App-4.summary: App-4 is a single added block of about 1750 lines (port lines 10813-12557) plus six insertions in handleCommand's head (12559-12620). The block holds 7 new worker threads (media watcher, buffer events, buffer safety stop, storage pre-roll, drive trim, clip merge, controls worker), the media record gate, playback hold rule, media profile and tuning helper calls, and the Controls-page backend (a second, pre-lock command dispatcher with get_controls, controls_history, controls_last_input, scan_i2c, list_actions; test_input; applyHardwareText restarting driver groups on save). No upstream code is removed. The only original code touched is handleCommand's head, extended in place: pre-lock dispatch, yield-window open, delete/pre-roll refusals, media gate, waitForMediaTrim/waitForClipMerge. Blame: d44b177 (19-commit squash, 537 lines), dcf09ee 348, ba0658d 317, 438a342 111, c34f844 68, 0a98868 67, 26da30e 55, 166cc4d 46, f5a61b8 44, f91fafa 42, 1319967 25. All fork-only; most Pi-tested only, 26da30e recorded "not tested". Upstream has no watcher, trim, merge, pre-roll, buffer events or controls worker, and no repo-side root helper scripts (it does call sudo -n libexec helpers for standby). Board assumptions are heavy: CFexpress hat on I2C bus 10 addr 0x34, NVMe over PCIe sysfs, exFAT, /home/pi paths, /usr/local/libexec helpers, 28-line header GPIO chip, I2C default bus 1, systemd unit names. The hint's "boot config" does not appear in this slice.

HW-controls-model.summary: The port adds seven new files to src/hardware: ActionCatalog, ControlsModel, ButtonGesture, GpioChipInfo (.hpp/.cpp) and I2cProbe (.hpp/.cpp). These drive the Controls page and the Hardware status cards. The catalog replaces upstream's three per-class normalizeSingleAction copies, plus the Grove target and trigger-event lists. ButtonGesture adds click and hold counting with Cinemate timing. ControlsModel builds the page rows and the settings spec. The chip setting is not on the Controls page: ControlsModel.hpp:263 says chip stays text-only. The same is true for poll_ms, open_drain and the output sections' chip key. The chip is still read from file by GpioInput, TriggerOutput and RecordingIndicatorOutput as upstream does. The status card passes the chip value unchanged to open(), so a value like gpiochip4 without /dev/ fails. The line list is cut at 28 lines and the free-pin list is fixed at BCM 4..27, which does not suit a microcontroller chip. gpioChipScore moved to GpioChipInfo.cpp for GpioInput, but TriggerOutput and RecordingIndicatorOutput keep their own copies. No host test covers any of this unit. The fork-log marks every commit fork-only, with "desk, pi build" as the test status. Apertar-Core is clean at 01f170c, so no chip row exists in the repo yet. Full tables are in the report file.

board_assumptions.what: RP1 / Pi 5 chip is scored first, then BCM pin controllers
Only /dev/gpiochip0..9 are scanned
The 40-pin header is 28 lines; free pins are fixed at BCM 4..27, with 2 and 3 as I2C bus 1
I2C bus 1 is the default for NeoRotary 0x49, PCF8574 0x20 and Grove 0x04
CFexpress hat on I2C bus 10 at 0x34 (a Pi 5 RP1 bus; probably absent on Pi 4)
NVMe on PCIe: /sys/class/nvme transport == pcie, link speed and width
I2C buses read from /sys/bus/i2c/devices because /sys/class/i2c-adapter is missing 'on this kernel'
The probe error text says the bus does not exist 'on this Pi'
scan_i2c address names assume Apertar sensors (0x1a), INA219, MPU6050 and the hat
Four cores, RAM size and fan are not referenced in this unit

HW-input-classes.summary: The port adds click/hold gestures (new ButtonGesture.hpp), 1-0-1 inversion, kernel edge events (the GpioInput poll loop is rewritten around poll()), [gpio_switches], and Listen seen-callbacks to the GPIO, PCF8574 and NeoRotary4 input classes. The three duplicated normalizeSingleAction alias chains, the Grove target aliases, the Trigger event aliases and one gpioChipScore copy move into new shared headers (ActionCatalog.hpp, GpioChipInfo.cpp); two gpioChipScore copies remain. Mpu6050RecordingSession.cpp lost 257 lines because its two private file-rewriting helpers (writeHardwareConfigValue and updateImuBiasConfig, about 230 lines) were replaced by HardwareConfigStore edits; the line-edit logic now lives in the new HardwareConfigText.hpp (1141 lines) and HardwareConfigStore.cpp (505 lines). Fork-log: every commit is fork-only and tested at the desk plus a Pi compile; no real button, switch, PCF, NeoRotary or edge-event hardware test is recorded. Behaviour changes: buttons held at start are now inverted instead of already-pressed, the IMU writes always go to ~/apertar-hardware.conf rather than the file the loader found, and the poll loop is replaced by an edge-event wait. Full tables in the report file.

features.name: Click and hold gestures on GPIO buttons
features.operator_gets: A GPIO button can run separate actions for press, single, double, triple click and 3 s hold, with Cinemate SmartButton timing.

features.tested: fork-log: fork-only; commit says desk only (click counter 8 checks), Pi build is first compile; no hardware run

features.name: Gestures on encoder pushes, NeoRotary pushes and PCF pins

features.tested: fork-log: fork-only; desk (host 120/121) plus Pi build; no hardware test recorded

features.name: 1-0-1 (normally closed) buttons

features.name: Edge events instead of polling
features.operator_gets: The GPIO input thread sleeps until a pin changes or a timer is due instead of waking every few ms; chips without edge events fall back to poll_ms.
features.relation_to_upstream: replaces upstream code (GpioInput::run poll loop becomes a poll()/read loop with process and sleepMs lambdas)
features.tested: fork-log: fork-only; desk (gesture fed only at edges) plus Pi build; no hardware run recorded

features.tested: fork-log: fork-only; desk (host 118/119) plus Pi build; no hardware run

features.name: Listen: inputs report what fired
